The school districts acting jointly shall submit to the Mayor and Board of
Trustees for their approval, not less than once every five (5) years, a revised
table of population density.
      4.   Subdivider's Alternative Demographic Study: In the event a
subdivider or developer files a written objection to the table of Estimated
Student Population Per Dwelling Unit listed in this Section, he shall submit
his own demographic study showing the estimated additional population to be
generated from the subdivision or planned unit development and in that event,
final determination of the density formula to be used in such calculation shall
be made by the Village Board of Trustees based upon such demographic
information submitted by the subdivider or developer and from other sources
which may be submitted to the Village Board of Trustees by the school district,
or others. It is recognized that population density, age distribution and local
conditions change over the years, and the specific formula for the dedication
of land, or the payment of fees in lieu thereof, as stated herein, is subject
to periodic review and amendment if necessary.
      5.   Reservation Of Additional Land: Where the Comprehensive Plan of the
Village calls for a larger amount of school sites in a particular proposed
subdivision or planned unit development than the developer is required to
dedicate, the land needed beyond the subdivider's or developer's contribution
shall, if so determined by the Village Board of Trustees, be reserved for
subsequent purchase by the Village or other public body designated by the
Village provided that such acquisition is made within one year from the date of
approval of the final plat.
      6.   Topography And Grading: The slope, topography and geology of the
dedicated site as well as its surroundings must be suitable for its intended
purposes. Grading on sites dedicated for school sites shall not differ greatly
from surrounding land.
      7.   Improved Sites: All sites shall be dedicated in a condition ready
for full service of electrical, water, sewer and streets as applicable to the
location of the site, or acceptable provision made therefor. The sidewalks and
trees normally included within the definition of improved sites may be deleted
due to the delay time between dedication of any such school sites and
construction of school facilities thereon.
      8.   Title To Sites: All sites shall be conveyed either by warranty or
trustee's deed for the benefit of the affected school district and conveyed
directly to the School Trustees. The subdivider or developer shall be
responsible for conveying good, merchantable title to such sites, and shall be
responsible for payment of all real estate taxes to the date of conveyance,
including any agricultural roll-back taxes which might be extended or levied
against such sites for any tax years or periods prior to the time of
conveyance.
      9.   Use Of Parcel: When, in the opinion of the school district holding
title to any parcel of land dedicated under this Section, any such parcel has
become unnecessary or unsuitable or inconvenient, such parcel may be sold as
provided by applicable statutory authority, and the proceeds shall be held in
trust by said unit of local government, solely for such uses as are provided
for in this Section, and said proceeds shall be subject to the ten (10) year
expenditure requirements from and after the date when said land is converted to
cash proceeds.
All dedications shall be made at the time of final plan approval and all cash
contributions required herein shall be made prior to the issuance of each
building permit by the Village.
If any provision of this Section, or the application thereof to any person or
circumstance, is declared invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, such
partial invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this
Section which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application
thereof, and to this extent the provisions of this Section are declared to be
severable. (Ord. 720, 8-28-1995)
***** CHAPTER 5
REQUIRED LAND IMPROVEMENTS *****
SECTION:
11-5-1:Scope
11-5-2:Sanitary Sewers
11-5-3:Storm Sewers
11-5-4:Water Supply
11-5-5:House Services
11-5-6:Street Improvements
11-5-7:Monuments And Markers
11-5-8:Protection And Repair Of Existing Improvements
11-5-9:Acceptance Of Streets And Improvements
11-5-10:Inspection At Subdivider's Expense
11-5-1: SCOPE:
Before a final plat of subdivision is approved by the board of trustees, the
owner or subdivider shall submit to the village engineer completed plans and
specifications, prepared by a registered engineer of the state of Illinois,
covering the improvements and utilities described in the subdivider's plat, and
the village engineer shall certify in writing to the board of trustees that
such improvements and utilities meet the minimum requirements of the village,
county, state, and other authorities having jurisdiction, and comply with the
following requirements of this chapter. (Ord. 468, 11-8-1976)
11-5-2: SANITARY SEWERS:
   (A)   Sanitary sewers and sanitary sewer services shall be installed to
serve all properties in the subdivision.
   (B)   Sanitary sewer systems shall be designed and constructed in accordance
with the requirements of the village. Sanitary and storm sewer systems shall
not be combined.
   (C)   Sewers may be placed only in public rights of way or in easements,
including easements in private streets.
   (D)   Sewer mains, with house service stubs to each lot, shall be
constructed prior to the construction of street pavements. Service stubs shall
be installed at the centerline of each lot and shall extend to within one foot
(1') of the front lot line.
   (E)   Where sanitary sewer mains of larger capacity than necessary are
required, as directed by the board of trustees to serve the subdivision as
delineated in the preliminary plat, the subdivider shall be required to pay for
the proportionate benefit of the installation of his subdivision, as
established by the board of trustees.
   (F)   Materials, system arrangements and details of design shall be subject
to the approval of the village board of trustees. (Ord. 468, 11-8-1976)
11-5-3: STORM SEWERS:
   (A)   Design: Adequate provisions shall be made in all subdivisions for the
proper drainage of storm water. The design of the drainage system within the
development shall anticipate and provide capacity for other drainage from
naturally tributary land. Such design shall provide adequate capacity for
transmitting such drainage from the other tributary areas on the basis of the
ultimate development of such other tributary areas, but such drainage system
need not make provision for the retention of other tributary areas, except as
may be required by the board of trustees.
   (B)   Prohibitions: Open ditches shall be prohibited, except where they may
be required in state or county rights of way, or as may otherwise be approved
by the village board of trustees.
   (C)   Drainage: Any outfall storm sewer that drains into an existing open
ditch or natural watercourse shall have a concrete headwall and a concrete
apron installed in accordance with village standards and specifications.
   (D)   Drain Inlets: Drain inlets shall be placed in the street gutters at
all intersections and elsewhere as required by the terrain, but shall not be
spaced more than six hundred feet (600') nor less than four hundred feet (400')
apart along the gutter.
   (E)   Sanitary Sewer System: Storm water shall not be directed into the
sanitary sewer system and no connections between the storm and sanitary sewer
systems will be permitted at any time before, during or after construction.
(Ord. 468, 11-8-1976)
   (F)   Sump Pump Discharge Line Connection To Storm Sewer: Any residential
sump pump ejector lines installed or replaced in or under a lot that abuts a
storm sewer system shall discharge only directly into village approved
subterranean drain tile that is connected to the village storm sewer system.
All such ejector lines and drain tile shall be installed, connected and
maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois plumbing
code. A violation of this provision shall be considered a business offense and
shall be punishable by a fine not to exceed fifty dollars ($50.00) per day for
each day of noncompliance. In addition, any violation of this provision shall
authorize the denial of a certificate of occupancy until the sump pump
discharge connection complies herewith. (Ord. 970, 8-25-2003)
11-5-4: WATER SUPPLY:
   (A)   The subdivider shall provide the subdivision with a complete water
main supply system which shall be connected to the public water supply system,
except that when good and sufficient reason can be demonstrated that such
connection cannot be made, the subdivider shall provide an individual water
supply on each lot in the subdivision in accordance with the requirements of
the Will County health department.
   (B)   Water transmission mains shall not be less than six inches (6") in
diameter, and shall be arranged so as to avoid dead ends. Shutoff valves shall
be provided at each branch main connection and elsewhere as required to permit
adequate sectionalizing for maintenance purposes.
   (C)   Fire hydrants shall be installed throughout the entire subdivision
when served by a public water supply system. Water mains shall be not less than
six inches (6") in diameter, and shall include installation of shutoff valves
and fire hydrants. Fire hydrants shall be installed at intervals of not to
exceed three hundred feet (300'). All fire hydrants shall have a six inch (6")
barrel and shall be provided with two (2) 21/2-inch hose connections and one
steamer connection.
   (D)   Where installation of water mains of larger capacity than required to
serve only the subdivision as delineated in the preliminary plan, the
subdivider shall install the larger size main, but shall be required to pay for
only the proportionate benefit of the installation that directly serves his
subdivision, as established by the board of trustees. (Ord. 468, 11-8-1976)
11-5-5: HOUSE SERVICES:
   (A)   House services for sewer and water shall be constructed to connect
with the utility service mains constructed within any street to serve each
adjoining lot, tract or building site. Such house services shall extend from
the main to a point of at least eight feet (8') beyond the outside curb lines
of the proposed roadway pavement in the street.
   (B)   House water service for each single-family residence shall be a
minimum of one inch (1"), type K copper or approved equal and shall be
terminated at a shutoff valve and box of a type approved by the village
engineer. In no case shall the buffalo box be located in the sidewalk or
driveway or be buried underground. (Ord. 468, 11-8-1976)
      1.   Buffalo Box Location: Each new buffalo box (commonly referred to as
a "B box") installed for the purpose of providing a potable water shut off
point shall be located at a point that lies seven feet (7') from the property
line and toward the right of way. A violation of this provision shall be
considered a business offense and shall be punishable by a fine not to exceed
fifty dollars ($50.00) per day for each day of noncompliance. In addition, any
violation of this provision shall authorize the denial of a certificate of
occupancy until a buffalo box is connected as required herewith. (Ord. 970, 8-
25-2003)
   (C)   House services for each multiple family, commercial or industrial
building shall be of the size and material as specified by the Village Engineer
and approved by the Village Board.
   (D)   The minimum size of sanitary house service connection from the main to
the sanitary house drain shall be six inch (6') vitrified tile.
   (E)   Upon completion of construction of all such house sewer and water
service connections with the utility mains, the subdivider shall prepare and
file with the Village Clerk accurate plans showing the exact location of all
such sewer and water mains, together with manholes, shut-off valves, and
similar facilities being a part thereof.
11-5-6: STREET IMPROVEMENTS:
   (A)   Streets: All streets, curbs and gutters shall be designed and
constructed in each new subdivision in conformance with the requirements and
specifications as approved by the Village Engineer and the Board of Trustees.
   (B)   Sidewalks and Pedestrian Ways: Sidewalks shall be installed in all
residential and commercial subdivisions and shall be constructed in accordance
with Village standards and specifications. The sidewalks shall be constructed
of Portland Cement concrete to a thickness of five inches (5") and to a width
of not less than four feet six inches (4'6") in residential districts and six
feet (6') in commercial districts. Sidewalks shall be located within the street
right of way one foot (1') from the abutting property line.
   (C)   Street Trees: Trees shall be planted along all streets where trees do
do not exist. Trees shall have a trunk diameter, measured twelve inches (12")
above the ground, of not less than two and one-half inches (21/2") and shall be
spaced not more than fifty feet (50') apart. This requirement will be satisfied
if an equivalent number of trees of the same size or larger are planted in a
naturalistic manner in the front yards of the adjoining lots. The plantings
shall be restricted to thornless honey locusts, sugar maples, pin oaks,
sycamores, and/or any other trees approved by the Village Board of Trustees.
Box elder, catalpa, cottonwood, elm, hackberry, poplar, willow and similar
brittle-wood species shall not be permitted for planting in any area devoted to
public use.
   (D)   Street Lighting: Street lighting shall be provided by the subdivider
throughout the subdivision at all street intersections and at intervals of not
more than three hundred feet (300') between intersections. The specific
locations, type of light standard, luminaires, and method of installation shall
be approved by the Village Engineer.
   (E)   Street Signs: An appropriate street sign shall be erected at each
street intersection within the subdivision. The type of sign and the location
thereof shall be subject to the approval and direction of the Village Engineer.
   (F)   Public Utilities: All utility distribution lines for telephone,
electric and TV cable service shall be placed undergound throughout each new
subdivision. Said distribution lines shall be placed within easements or
dedicated public ways, in a manner which will not conflict with other
underground services. Further, all transformer boxes shall be located so as not
to be unsightly or hazardous to the public.
   (G)   As-Built Plans: Upon completion of the installation of improvements in
a subdivision, one set of tracings on cloth or equal suitable for use in
reproduction, which shows all improvements as actually installed in the field,
shall be filed with the Village Clerk.
11-5-7: MONUMENTS AND MARKERS:
Monuments shall be placed at all corners and angle points of the outside
boundary but no further than one-quarter (1/4) mile apart. The monuments shall
be of concrete, not less than six inches (6") in diameter and thirty six inches
(36") deep, with a center copper dowel three inches (3") long cast in place.
Iron pipe or steel bars not less than three-quarter inch (3/4") in diameter and
thirty six inches (36") long shall be set at the intersection of street
centerlines and at all corners of lots not marked by monuments.
11-5-8: PROTECTION AND REPAIR OF EXISTING IMPROVEMENTS:
The subdivider, his contractors, and suppliers shall be jointly and severally
responsible for taking any necessary precautions to insure that existing
improvements and property in the Village of Beecher are not damaged or rendered
unsightly by the operations of the subdivider, the suppliers, or contractors.
This provision is intended to include damage or nuisance with respect to land
improvements or landscaping in the Village of Beecher, damage to existing
streets, sidewalks, curbs and gutters, or parkways by passage thereover of
equipment or trucks, or by excavation of any purpose; the spillage or tracking
of earth, sand or rock onto existing streets, sidewalks, curb and gutter, or
parkways; the washing by storm water of earth or sand onto streets, sidewalks,
curb and gutter or catch basins; and damage to water mains, sanitary sewers,
culverts, or storm sewers. To reduce or localize the possibility of damage to
streets by heavy trucking, the Village President shall instruct the subdivider
as to the streets to be used for access to the subdivision by equipment and
trucks and the subdivider shall be responsible for enforcement of this
instruction upon his contractors and their suppliers. Where deemed advisable,
the Village President shall also have the power to require, either prior to
commencement of construction, or after construction is in progress, that the
subdivider posts a surety bond in sufficient amount to guarantee repair of
damages or abatement of nuisance. Where need for surety becomes apparent after
construction is in process, the Village President shall have the power to order
construction discontinued until surety has been posted. Expenses incurred by
the Village in repairing damages, cleaning streets, catch basins and sewers
shall be deducted from the surety.
11-5-9: ACCEPTANCE OF STREETS AND IMPROVEMENTS:
Acceptance of streets and improvements is conditional, based upon a one year
maintenance period which commences with the formal date of acceptance of the
streets by the Village Board. A maintenance bond running to the Village Board
is required to be written and accepted by the Village Board at such time as the
streets and improvements are accepted. The amount of the maintenance bond shall
be one-fourth (1/4) the estimated cost of the streets and improvements and
shall be set by the Village Engineer. At the end of the one year period, if all
of the accepted improvements are in satisfactory condition, the maintenance
bond shall be released by the Village Board.
Final acceptance of all streets and improvements for maintenance shall be made
only by the adoption of a resolution by the Village Board of Trustees after
there has been filed with the Village Clerk a certificate or letter by the
Village Engineer certifying that all improvements required to be constructed or
installed, in connection with the approval of the final plat of subdivision,
have been fully completed and the construction or installation thereof has been
approved by him.
When the subdivider has completed the construction of the improvements he shall
notify the Village Engineer by letter (four copies) of this fact, and formally
request a final inspection by said party or a duly designated deputy. In this
letter he shall briefly describe all improvements and he shall enclose four (4)
copies of the subdivision plan which shows these improvements. No later than
fourteen (14) days after receipt of this letter by the Village Engineer he, or
a duly designated deputy, shall make his inspection. The fee shall be
determined by the Village Board.
No later than fourteen (14) days after inspection of the subdivision
improvements, the subdivider shall be notified by the Village Engineer in
writing of the results of the inspection.
11-5-10: INSPECTION AT SUBDIVIDER'S EXPENSE:
All public improvements required to be made under the provisions of this
Chapter shall be inspected during the course of construction by the Village
Engineer or a duly designated deputy. All fees and costs connected with such
inspection and the reviewing of the plans and specifications for such
improvements shall be paid by the subdivider to the Village. All inspection
fees shall be paid before release of any bonds and such fees shall not exceed
one and one-half percent (11/2%) of the cost of construction of said
improvements inspected. (Ord. 468, 11-8-76)
***** CHAPTER 6
ADMINISTRATION; ENFORCEMENT *****
SECTION:
11-6-1:Plan Commission to Administer
11-6-2:Use of Professional Assistance
11-6-3:Building Permit
11-6-4:Occupancy Permit
11-6-5:Variations
11-6-6:Enforcement
11-6-7:Record of Plats
11-6-8:Violation Penalty
11-6-1: PLAN COMMISSION TO ADMINISTER:
The provisions of this Title shall be administered by the Plan Commission
acting in lieu of the Village Board of Trustees, except as specifically
provided in this Ordinance.
11-6-2: USE OF PROFESSIONAL ASSISTANCE:
The Plan Commission and Village Board may utilize the services of outside
professionals to assist them in the technical review and processing of proposed
plats of subdivision. The subdivider shall, in addition to the fees outlined in
Section
11-1-8 of this Title, reimburse the Village for any planning, engineering and
legal expenses incurred by it in connection with the review of plans and
specifications, preparing and checking cost estimates, examining agreements,
and furnishing of opinions and other professional advice as may be required.
Such costs shall be paid to the Village Clerk.
11-6-3: BUILDING PERMIT:
No building permit shall be issued by any governing official for the
construction of any building, structure or improvement to the land or any lot
within a subdivision as defined herein, which has been approved for platting or
replatting, until all requirements of this Title have been complied with -
unless an agreement is entered into between the builder or owner and the
Village waiving or postponing such requirements.
11-6-4: OCCUPANCY PERMIT:
No occupancy permit shall be granted by any governing official for the use of
any building or structure within a subdivision approved for platting or
replatting until required utility facilities have been installed and made ready
to service the property, and until roadways providing access to the subject lot
or lots have been constructed or are in the course of construction and are
suitable for vehicular traffic.
11-6-5: VARIATIONS:
The Plan Commission may recommend variances from the literal application of the
requirements in specific cases which, in its opinion, do not affect the general
plan or spirit of the Title. Requests for such variations shall be made in
writing to the Plan Commission by the subdivider. In recommending any variance,
the Plan Commission shall specify conditions necessary to assure that the
proposed subdivision: (1) will not be detrimental to the neighborhood and to
the community as a whole; (2) complies with the intent of this Title; (3)
complies with the comprehensive plan of the Village; and (4) does not violate
any other ordinances or regulations of the Village.
11-6-6: ENFORCEMENT:
No plat of any subdivision shall be entitled to be recorded in the County
Recorder's office or have any validity until it shall have been approved in a
manner prescribed in this Title. The Building Commissioner of the Village of
Beecher shall be responsible for the enforcement of these subdivision
regulations. Said commissioner shall have the power and shall see that the
provisions herein are properly enforced.
11-6-7: RECORD OF PLATS:
The Village Clerk shall keep a record of all final plats approved by the
Village Board showing the date of approval, the date of recordation, the
subdivision name, the legal description of the property involved, and any
pertinent data or information related thereto. This record shall be available
for inspection by the public during regular business hours.
11-6-8: VIOLATION PENALTY:
Any person, firm or corporation found guilty of violating any of the provisions
of this Title shall be fined not less than twenty five dollars ($25.00) nor
more than two hundred dollars ($200.00) for each violation, plus the cost of
action, and each day that such violation continues shall be deemed to be a
separate offense. (Ord. 468, 11-8-76)
***** CHAPTER 7
GENERAL STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS *****
SECTION:
11-7-1:Standards and Specifications
11-7-1: STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS:
   (A)   Major Thoroughfares: Eighty (80) to one hundred (100) foot right of
way, cross sections in accordance with the comprehensive plan and/or official
map and as determined by the Village Engineer and the Plan Commission.
   (B)   Collector Thoroughfares: Eighty foot (80') right of way, forty two
foot (42') pavements, sidewalks per Village specifications.
   (C)   Minor Streets: No on-street parking, sixty six foot (66') right of
way, thirty two foot (32') pavements, sidewalks per Village specifications.
   (D)   Streets Along Development Boundaries and Streets Connecting
Development with Existing Improved Street System: Cross sections are determined
by the Village Engineer and the Plan Commission.
   (E)   Alleys: Paved full width per Village specifications.
   (F)   Lot and Street Grading: Per plans and profiles approved by the Village
Engineer. Top of foundation elevations shall be noted.
   (G)   Curb and Gutter: Portland cement concrete per typical section, exhibit
A.
   (H)   Storm sewers must be provided. Curb inlets shall be provided at an
interval not to exceed six hundred feet (600'). The storm sewers must be
constructed in accordance with Section 603 "Storm Sewers" of the Standard
Specifications.
   (I)   Street Pavement Base:
      1.   The base course shall be constructed in strict compliance with
Section 301 "Aggregate Base Course" of the standard specifications.
      2.   Prior to surfacing, the developer must obtain and provide to the
Village a compaction test and thickness coring report. The compaction test
shall be taken at intervals not to exceed three hundred feet (300') in length
or as directed by the Village Engineer. Corings shall be taken at the center-
line and adjacent to the curb at intervals not to exceed five hundred feet
(500') in length or as directed by the Village Engineer.
   (J)   Street Pavement: The surface course shall be constructed in strict
compliance with Section 405 "Bituminous Surface Plantmix" (Class B) of the
standard specifications, with the following exceptions: The surface course
shall be laid in two (2) layers. The first layer shall be one and one-half
inches (11/2") compacted thickness. The surface layer shall be one inch (1")
compacted thickness, and the aggregate shall be modified to that called for in
bituminous concrete surface courses.
   (K)   Driveways: Per Village specifications.
   (L)   Sidewalks: Five inches (5") thick and four feet (4') wide Portland
cement concrete in accordance with typical section, exhibit A.
   (M)   Trees: One inch (1") minimum caliper, forty feet (40') to fifty feet
(50') apart per Village specifications. Required within front yard setback. No
trees or shrubs will be allowed in the parkway.
   (N)   All parkways must be top-soiled, seeded and mulched by the developer.
Slopes over 3:1 shall be sodded.
      (0)   Street Name Signs: At all intersections per Village specifications.
   (P)   Street Lighting: Street lighting shall be installed at all
intersections and at intervals of not more than three hundred feet (300')
between intersections. The specific locations, type of light standard,
luminaries, and method of installation shall be approved by the Village
Engineer. Poles shall be concrete or aluminum.
   (Q)   Telephone and Electric Service: In rear or side lot easements. These
utilities shall be installed undergound.
   (R)   Gas: In street planting strip.
   (S)   All cross road culverts shall be a minimum eighteen inches (18") in
diameter. All driveway culverts shall be a minimum of fifteen inches (15") in
diameter and must be placed a minimum of ten feet (10') distance from the edge
of the roadway. The driveway culvert shall not exceed twenty four feet (24') in
length. Each lot shall be limited to one driveway culvert, except in the case
of a circle drive where upon written request to the street chairman an
additional culvert may be authorized. All culverts shall be installed in
accordance with Section 511 "Pipe Culverts" of the standard specifications.
   (T)   All excavations within the curb lines shall be backfilled with
compacted granular material.
All plans and specifications for utility and street improvements shall be
prepared and certified by an Illinois Registered Professional Engineer. (Ord.
468, 11-8-76)

***** CHAPTER 1
GENERAL PROVISIONS *****
SECTION:

12-1-17:Notification When Moving From Premises
12-1-18:Penalties
12-1-1: JURISDICTION OF WATERWORKS AND SEWERAGE DEPARTMENT:
The waterworks and sewerage department, under the direction of the village
president and board of trustees, and such other officers and employees
designated by them shall have the supervision, management and control, subject
to the village board, of the maintenance, enlargement and operation of the
waterworks and sanitary sewer utility systems owned and controlled by the
village, and of all matters and things connected with the operation,
maintenance and extension of said systems and preserving the property belonging
thereto. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-2: DEFINITIONS:
Unless the context specifically indicates otherwise, the meaning of terms in
this title shall be as follows:
   MULTIPLE CONNECTION USER: Any additional number of residential or commercial
units located on a property being served through a single water meter where
there are no separate water meters for each unit, such as apartment buildings,
or commercial and residential units located within the same building.
   SEWER TAP-IN FEE: Those permit and/or inspection fees as specified in this
title.
   SINGLE-FAMILY HOMES: A single-family residential dwelling unit.
   SPECIAL MULTIPLE CONNECTION USER: Those structures or buildings having one
water meter and living quarters or rooms for overnight occupancy without a
specifically defined dwelling unit or consistent occupancy ratings such as
motels, hotels and nursing homes.
   WATER TAP-IN FEE: The permit and inspection fees as specified in this title.
(Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-3: REPORTS:
   (A)   A written monthly operations report shall be prepared and submitted,
not later than the fifth day of each and every month or more often or less as
required, through the village administrator to the board of trustees including,
but not limited to, the following:
      1.   Volume of water pumped and treated;
      2.   Treatment usage;
      3.   Number of hydrants flushed;
      4.   New services installed;
      5.   Number of meters changed or installed; and
      6.   Details of any major repairs and extensions to mains or other
pertinent information.
   (B)   A written monthly financial report shall be prepared and submitted,
not later than the twenty eighth day of each and every month or more often or
less as required, through the village administrator to the board of trustees
including, but not limited to, the following:
      1.   Water and sewer billing register;
      2.   Collections;
      3.   Expenditures and accounts charged;
      4.   Cash balances at beginning and end of period;
      5.   Volume of water purchased, billed and unaccounted for;
      6.   New service fees received; and
      7.   Number of metered and unmetered customers connected to the system at
the beginning and the end of reporting period. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-4: BOOKS OF ACCOUNTS:
The village treasurer shall keep, or cause to be kept, full and complete books
of accounts separate and apart from any other records of the village showing in
detail all monies received by the village with dates and sources and all
matters pertaining to his office in a clear and generally accepted manner. The
treasurer shall also keep such other books as the board of trustees may from
time to time direct. All such books, accounts and papers pertaining to said
office shall at all reasonable times be open to the inspection of the board of
trustees, any member thereof, and the holder of any outstanding waterworks and
sewerage revenue bonds. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-5: BANK DEPOSITS:
The village office manager, or designee, shall, not later than five (5)
business days after the receipt thereof, deposit into the properly authorized
village accounts all monies collected by the village from any source
whatsoever, and provide a duplicate of the bank deposit ticket or receipt to
the village treasurer. The village office manager, or designee, is expressly
prohibited from retaining monies of the village in village offices or in any
account other than the proper bank account to the credit of the village and
within the time guidelines provided herein. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-6: VILLAGE ADMINISTRATOR DUTIES:
Under the general supervision of the village administrator, the village
employees shall read water meters, prepare and distribute bills, collect the
water and sanitary sewer fees, issue water and sanitary sewer permits, and
shall perform such other duties as now are or may hereafter be imposed upon the
administrator by the law or the ordinances of the village. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-
2006)
12-1-7: ACCESS TO PREMISES:
The superintendent, building inspector, and/or their respective designees,
shall have reasonable access at reasonable times to the premises, places, or
buildings served by the waterworks and sewerage systems and it shall be
unlawful for any person to interfere with, prevent, or obstruct said persons in
the exercise of their duties. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-8: RATES:
The services of the waterworks and sewerage systems are furnished to the
respective premises by the village only upon the condition that the owner of
the premises, the occupant thereof and the user of the service are jointly and
severally liable therefor to the village for the rates, charges, and permit
fees. All customers, users, or properties in the village shall pay such rates,
charges, and permit fees for the use and service of the waterworks and sewerage
systems in such manner and amounts as shall be prescribed by ordinance by the
president and board of trustees from time to time. The board of trustees may,
upon application by any person, grant a waiver or reduction to the commercial
or industrial rates, charges, and permit fees, based on the amount of water
consumed, tax valuation of property, and revenue potential for the village and
other similar data. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-9: WATER AND SEWER SERVICE OUTSIDE VILLAGE LIMITS:
Water or sanitary sewer services or connections to properties outside the
corporate limits may be allowed in such cases as determined by majority vote of
the corporate authorities. In the event of approval of such connections, all
such users of water and/or sanitary sewage services shall be charged an amount
as the corporate authorities so establish from time to time. However, such
rates and charges shall not be less than two hundred percent (200%) of the
prevailing rates for service provided within the corporate limits. No person
having a residence or place of business within the territorial limits of the
village shall be permitted to purchase water or sanitary sewer services from
any other municipal corporation or other public utility for such residence or
place of business located in the village whenever the waterworks and/or
sewerage system of the village is adjacent to the property to be provided by
the utility services.
Any person owning or controlling premises located outside the corporate limits
of the village and desiring to connect to the waterworks and sanitary sewerage
systems of the village after village approval as provided above, may do so by
complying with the requirements of this title and by paying connection fees as
determined by the board of trustees and by paying the water and sewer bills
submitted to them by the village. If the property to be served is adjacent to
the village, the applicant must agree to annex to the village, otherwise the
corporate authorities have the right to refuse sewer and/or water service.
(Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-10: PERMIT APPLICATION; CONNECTIONS:
No person shall install or repair any sanitary sewer or water main without
first obtaining a written permit for such work from the village. Any person
desiring to make any connection to the water and/or sanitary sewer system shall
first make application to the village upon a blank form or forms furnished by
the village. Said application shall contain an agreement on the part of the
applicant that all the rules, regulations, conditions and provisions of any
ordinance relating to the waterworks system or sewerage system will be complied
with; that all water rates, sewer rates, assessments and rents and all fines
and penalties assessed, charged or imposed against said applicant upon the
property described in said application will be paid. When the applicant
hereunder has complied with all of the provisions of the ordinances of the
village, a permit shall then be issued by the village authorizing the
connection to be made and specifying the size thereof. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-11: PERMIT FEES:
The fees to be charged for a permit to tap or otherwise make a connection with
any water or sanitary sewer main shall be determined in such manners and
amounts as shall be prescribed by ordinance adopted by the president and board
of trustees from time to time. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-12: WATER OR SEWER CONNECTION:
All connections made to the waterworks and sewerage systems made by a licensed
contractor shall be made under the supervision of the superintendent thereof,
and no connection shall be covered until the work has been inspected and
approved. A utility connection or extension shall be accomplished by boring
only beneath the road and sidewalk and any open cutting is not allowed except
by special permit of the village. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-13: LICENSED CONTRACTORS:
Whenever a permit for a connection to the water or sewer mains of the village
is issued hereunder, a connection may only be permitted by a contractor who has
on file in the office of the village a properly executed bond, certificate of
liability coverage, and security deposit, as follows:
   (A)   Performance Bond: A licensed contractor shall have filed in the office
of the village clerk a performance bond with corporate surety thereon in the
sum of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) for sewer connections and/or a house
connection; and for a sewer or water extension, a sum equal to one and one-half
(11/2) times the estimated cost of the work to be done. Such performance bond
shall be approved by the village, conditioned upon the applicant indemnifying
and saving harmless the village for any and all damage to underground utilities
or to the water and sewer mains and laterals of the village and from any
failure to restore any road, ditch, pavement or portion thereof damaged during
the construction of the utility connection or extension so as to leave said
road, ditch, pavement or portion thereof damaged in as good condition as said
applicant or contractor found them.
   (B)   Insurance: A licensed contractor shall file in the office of the
village clerk a certificate of public liability insurance in an amount not less
than fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) for injuries, including accidental
death, to any one person and subject to the same limit for each person in an
amount not less than one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) on account of
one accident, and property damage insurance in an amount not less than fifty
thousand dollars ($50,000.00). The persons to be indemnified and saved harmless
in said insurance policy shall be the village and the applicant for utility
connection or extension. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-14: UTILITY WORK IN STREETS:
   (A)   All public utility companies desiring to install any public utility
under any street or alley in the village shall auger/bore under the village
streets for installation of the public utility. Cutting of a public street or
alley by a public utility is prohibited unless written authorization by the
village is obtained.
The public utility must notify the village superintendent prior to the auguring
or installation of the utility and all open holes made as a result of such
auguring must be properly barricaded and warning lights installed prior to the
workmen leaving the area. The public utility must restore any excavations to
the original ground condition upon completion of any installation.
   (B)   Open trench cutting of existing village streets or alleys shall be
allowed for connecting a private sewer and water line to the existing village
sewer and water system, but only under the following terms and conditions:
      1.   The superintendent of public works must be contacted for approval
prior to the trench cut and shall inspect all cuts, backfilling, and surface
patching.
      2.   The trench cut into the village street (asphalt or concrete) shall
be saw cut prior to excavating.
      3.   For a period not to exceed five (5) years, the owner or contractor
must deposit an escrow of two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500.00) cash
(or cash equivalent, example: certified check and money order) with the village
until inspected and accepted by the village. The escrowed funds or any portion
of them may be used by the village to restore the trenched area. Further, the
village may retain a portion of the escrow for future maintenance for an
additional two (2) years. After the five (5) year period or acceptance by the
village, whichever is earlier, any remaining escrow funds will be returned to
the depositor. No interest will be paid to the depositor on the escrowed funds.
      4.   All openings made in streets and sidewalks shall be protected at all
times in the following manner: Open holes or trenches shall not exist
overnight, but must be backfilled and sufficiently barricaded with signal or
warning lights prior to the work crew leaving the area for the day.
      5.   Compliance with the subdivision ordinance regulations and
requirements for the installation of water and sanitary sewer lines and
connections. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-15: WATER AND SEWER CONNECTION COSTS:
   (A)   Cost Borne By Owner: All costs and expenses incident to the
installation and connection of the building water and sanitary sewer services
shall be borne by the property owner. The property owner shall indemnify the
village for any loss or damage that may directly or indirectly be occasioned by
the installation of the building water and sewer services and the maintenance
thereof.
   (B)   Emergency Repairs: The village may, in case of emergency, repair or
order the repair of any sewer or water line from the village sewer and water
mains to the premises served thereby, and if it does so, the cost of such
repair work shall be repaid to the village by the property owner, which cost
shall be treated and collected in the same manner and with the same remedies as
for collection of charges for water and sewer services.
   (C)   Repairs By Water And Sewer Department: Any maintenance or repair work
performed by the water and sewer department of the village on any water or
sewer line shall be paid for by the owner or the occupant (both of whom shall
be liable for the cost thereof) of the property served by such line at the
current hourly rate paid by the village to its employees or contractors. (Ord.
1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-16: PROTECTION FROM DAMAGE:
No person shall maliciously, wilfully or negligently break, damage, destroy,
uncover, deface or tamper with any structure, appurtenance or equipment which
is a part of the waterworks or sewage systems. Any person violating this
provision shall be subject to immediate arrest under charge of disorderly
conduct and subject to fines and penalties as provided herein as well as the
cost to repair or replace the damage caused by the person. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-
2006)
12-1-17: NOTIFICATION WHEN MOVING FROM PREMISES:
Any person or party who shall vacate any premises, or any party who shall enter
upon and occupy any premises, shall immediately, before vacating said premises
or moving to said premises, notify the village and secure reading of the water
meter. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-1-18: PENALTIES:
   (A)   Unless otherwise provided in this title, any person found to be
violating any provisions of this title shall be served by the village with
written notice stating the nature of the violation and providing a reasonable
time limit for the satisfactory correction thereof. The offender shall, within
the period of time stated in such notice, permanently cease all violations.
   (B)   Any person who shall continue any violation beyond the time limit
provided for in subsection (A) of this section shall be guilty of a
misdemeanor, and on conviction thereof shall be fined in the amount not less
than twenty five dollars ($25.00) and not to exceed seven hundred fifty dollars
($750.00) for each violation. Each day in which any such violation shall
continue shall be deemed as a separate offense.
   (C)   Additionally, any person violating any of the provisions of this
chapter shall become liable to the village for any expense, loss, or damage
occasioned by the village by reason of such violation, including reasonable
attorney fees and costs incurred in the enforcement of this title.
   (D)   The village reserves the right to discontinue sewer and/or water
service to any property found in violation of this title until such time as the
violation is rectified and any charges or penalties are paid in full. (Ord.
1053, 11-14-2006)
***** CHAPTER 2
WATERWORKS SYSTEM RULES AND REGULATIONS *****
SECTION:
12-2-1:Unauthorized Water Usage
12-2-2:Water Meter Regulations
12-2-3:Right Of Access
12-2-4:Water Main Connections
12-2-5:Water Service To Other Building
12-2-6:Connection To Standard Water Main Required
12-2-7:New Cross Connections Prohibited
12-2-8:Existing Cross Connections
12-2-1: UNAUTHORIZED WATER USAGE:
No person, unless duly authorized, shall turn on any water service cock, or use
water therefrom when so turned on under penalty of fine and additionally, said
person shall be liable for the regular water rates without discount for the
water used.
No seal placed by the village for the protection of any meter, valve, fitting,
hydrant, or other water connection shall be defaced or broken, except with
written authorization by the village.
No person or persons, other than the village and its employees, shall use water
from any fire hydrant connected with the village waterworks system, except for
extinguishing fires or unless specifically authorized by the village. (Ord.
1053, 11-14-2006)
12-2-2: WATER METER REGULATIONS:
   (A)   All water customers shall be supplied through village provided meters
only, which shall remain for all time the village's property, except that in
cases where it is temporarily impractical to set a meter, and the use and
consumption of water shall be governed by other applicable provisions of this
chapter. After the meter is placed, only officers or employees of the village
shall be allowed to repair, remove, or in any manner interfere with same. A
shutoff valve shall be placed on each side of the water meter by and at the
cost of the property owner.
   (B)   The ordinary cost of keeping each meter in repair shall be paid by the
village. The person upon whose application any meter is installed or the then
owner and/or occupant of the premises served shall be jointly and severally
liable for any breakage or damage done to such meter, including damage from
freezing, hot water, or breakage and also for the theft thereof and the cost of
making good such loss or damage shall be paid by the owner, and/or the
occupant, of the premises in which such meter was installed as soon as the bill
for same is presented and the amount thereof shall be a lien against the
premises for which said meter was installed to the extent and with the same
effect as water rates.
   (C)   It shall be unlawful for any person to injure, deface, mar, destroy,
or in any manner to interfere with any meter. It shall be the duty of the owner
or occupant to promptly notify the village of defects in the meter or of its
failure to properly register the quantity of water passing through same.
   (D)   Water meters shall be located at such places and in such manner as the
village shall direct within the premises to be served or in boxes or vaults,
and all such installations shall be made in accordance with the specifications
prescribed by the village, and such meter locations must be so situated as to
prevent freezing of water flowing through such meters.
   (E)   The installation of all new water meters shall be required to have
outside water meter reading equipment installed with the meter. All meters and
dials installed shall be furnished by the village and the cost shall be borne
by the property owner. Any existing meters not having outside water meter
reading equipment that require replacement shall be replaced with the outside
meter reading equipment and the cost of said reading equipment shall be borne
by the property owner.
   (F)   All water meters installed in the village for nonresidential buildings
and residential buildings with sprinkler systems shall have installed a
"backflow prevention device" as required by the state of Illinois plumbing
code. The "backflow prevention device" shall be of the kind and nature as
prescribed by the Illinois environmental protection agency and the state of
Illinois plumbing code and installed by a licensed plumbing contractor. The
installation of the "backflow prevention device" shall be at the cost of the
property owner. Further, annual inspections shall be completed by the owner of
the structure with a "backflow prevention device" and a copy of the inspection
shall be provided to the superintendent. The annual inspection shall determine
if the "backflow prevention device" is installed and operating properly. Due
the potential contamination of the village's water system, the superintendent
may immediately suspend water service to any structure with a "backflow
prevention device" that does not comply with the annual inspection requirements
as provided herein and the water service shall only be resumed after the annual
inspection has been completed and a copy of the results provided to the
superintendent. The property owner shall bear the cost of shutting off and
resuming water services and for the costs associated with the installation of
and annual inspection of the "backflow prevention device". (Ord. 1053, 11-14-
2006)
12-2-3: RIGHT OF ACCESS:
The superintendent, and designee, and all meter inspectors, shall have
reasonable access to the premises, place, or building where such meters are
located for the purpose of reading, examining, testing, and repairing same, and
examining and testing the consumption, use, and flow of water, and it shall be
unlawful for any person or corporation to interfere with, prevent, or obstruct
the superintendent or designee in the performance of the requirements herein.
(Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-2-4: WATER MAIN CONNECTIONS:
All corporation stops, goosenecks, curb stops, buffalo boxes and meter boxes
installed in connection with the waterworks system of the village must be
approved by the village prior to installation.
No person shall in any manner obstruct or cause to be obstructed the free
access of any duly authorized officer or employee of the village to any curb
stop, water meter, shutoff box or connection with any water main by means of
any concrete, lumber, brick, building material or by any other means or device
whatsoever or to use or to prevent free access thereto by such officer or
employee.
All repairs on water service pipes and plumbing systems of buildings from the
mains to the premises to be served shall be made by and at the expense of the
owners of the premises served. The village may, in case of emergency, repair
any water service pipes, plumbing systems and sewer service pipes, and if this
work is done the cost of such repair work shall be repaid to the village by the
owner of the premises served. The property owner is responsible for all repairs
from the buffalo box to the building within the property lines. (Ord. 1053, 11-
14-2006)
12-2-5: WATER SERVICE TO OTHER BUILDING:
No person, whether owner or occupant, in possession or control of any building,
structure or premises into which water is supplied through the village
waterworks system shall be allowed, without village administrator's written
authorization, to supply other persons or families or to supply water from such
building or premises to any other building structure or premises. The supply of
water to a building, structure or premises of any person who violates any of
the foregoing provisions of this section shall be shut off and ceased
immediately. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-2-6: CONNECTION TO STANDARD WATER MAIN REQUIRED:
In all cases where a standard water main is now installed or hereafter may be
installed in any street, alley, public way or easement in the village, all
water users located on any such street, alley, public way or easement shall
make or cause to be made connection to such standard water main and pay the
tapping charges within three (3) months after the installation of such standard
water main if the same be not now installed, and all users shall discontinue,
within the same period of time, any connection which they theretofore may have
had with any other water line. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-2-7: NEW CROSS CONNECTIONS PROHIBITED:
Whenever a system of water supply piping, either inside or outside of any
building, receives its supply from any source other than the waterworks system
of the village, such system shall be kept entirely separate from and no cross
connections or connections of any kind shall be made with any pipe or system of
piping which received its supply from the village waterworks system. Water
which has once been used for any purpose whatsoever shall not be returned to
the building's water supply system. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-2-8: EXISTING CROSS CONNECTIONS:
   (A)   Compliance Required: All plumbing within the village shall be
installed in accordance with the Illinois plumbing code, as amended or replaced
from time to time. If, in accordance with the Illinois plumbing code or in the
judgment of the building inspector, an approved "backflow prevention device" is
necessary for the safety of the public water supply system, the building
inspector will give notice to the water customer to install such an approved
device immediately. The water customer shall, at the customer's own expense,
install such an approved device at a location and in a manner in accordance
with all applicable regulations, and shall have inspections and tests made of
such approved devices upon installation and as required by all applicable
regulations.
   (B)   Approval Of Connection: No person shall establish or permit to be
established or maintain or permit to be maintained any connection whereby a
private, auxiliary or emergency water supply other than the regular public
water supply of the village may enter the supply or distribution system of the
village, unless such private, auxiliary or emergency water supply and the
method of connection and use of such supply shall have been approved by the
building inspector and the Illinois environmental protection agency.
   (C)   Surveys And Investigations Required: It shall be the duty of the
building inspector or superintendent to cause surveys and investigations to be
made of commercial, industrial and other properties served by the public water
supply to determine whether actual or potential hazards to the public water
supply may exist.
   (D)   Right Of Entry, Improper Connections: The village's cross connection
control device inspector shall have the right to enter at any reasonable time
any property served by a connection to the public water supply or distribution
system of the village for the purpose of verifying the presence or absence of
cross connections, and the superintendent, or designee, shall have the right to
enter at any reasonable time any property served by a connection to the public
water supply or distribution system of the village for the purpose of verifying
information submitted by the customer regarding the required cross connection
control inspection. On demand, the owner, lessees or occupants of any property
so served shall furnish to the superintendent, or designee, any information
which may be requested regarding the piping system or systems of water use on
such property. The refusal of such information, when demanded, shall, within
the discretion of the superintendent, or designee, be deemed evidence of the
presence of improper connections as provided in this section.
   (E)   Disconnection Of Service, Notice: The superintendent, or designee, is
hereby authorized and directed to discontinue, after reasonable notice to the
occupant thereof, the water service to any property wherein any connection in
violation of the provisions of this section is known to exist, and to take such
other precautionary measures as deemed necessary to eliminate any danger of
contamination of the public water supply distribution mains. Water service to
such property shall not be restored until such conditions have been eliminated
or corrected in compliance with the provisions of this section, and until a
reconnection fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) is paid to the village. Immediate
disconnection with verbal notice can be effected when the building inspector,
or superintendent, or designee, is assured that imminent danger of harmful
contamination of the public water supply system exists. Such action shall be
followed by written notification of the cause of the disconnection. Immediate
disconnection without notice to any party can be effected to prevent actual or
anticipated contamination or pollution of the public water supply; provided
that, in the reasonable opinion of the building inspector, superintendent, or
designee, or the Illinois environmental protection agency, such action is
required to prevent actual or potential contamination or pollution of the
public water supply. Neither the village or its agents or assigns shall be
liable to any customer for any injury, damages or lost revenues which may
result from termination of said customer's water supply in accordance with the
terms of this section, whether or not said termination was with or without
notice.
   (F)   Cost Of Cleanup: The customer responsible for backsiphoned or back
pressured material or contamination through backflow, if contamination of the
potable water supply system occurs through an illegal cross connection or an
improperly installed, maintained or repaired device, or a device which has been
bypassed, shall bear the cost of cleanup of the village potable water supply
system in addition to the fines and penalties provided in this title. (Ord.
1053, 11-14-2006)
***** CHAPTER 3
WATERWORKS PERMIT FEES, RATES, AND CHARGES *****
SECTION:
12-3-1:Rates And Charges
12-3-2:New Water Account Fee

12-3-1: RATES AND CHARGES:
   (A)   Based Upon Consumption: Each residential, commercial, industrial and/
or Municipal user of the water utility service shall pay rates and charges
based upon the amount of water consumed, as shown by the water meters, for each
bimonthly period, as follows:
      1.   Five dollar ($5.00) administrative fee;
      2.   Three dollar ($3.00) system maintenance fee;
      3.   One dollar ($1.00) debt service fee;
      4.   Four dollar ($4.00) flat water system infrastructure replacement fee
per billing period plus two dollars ($2.00) per one thousand (1,000) gallons of
water metered to be billed and collected. The water system infrastructure
replacement fee shall be transferred and deposited in the Water and Sewer
Capital Improvement Fund as an intrafund transfer at least once during each
fiscal year for the purposes of replacing aging water mains, valves, and
hydrants of the water distribution system;
      5.   High capacity user charge of one dollar ($1.00) per one thousand
(1,000) gallons of water metered after the first thirty thousand (30,000)
gallons for operations and maintenance; and
      6.   Five dollars fifteen cents ($5.15) operating expense fee per one
thousand (1,000) gallons of water metered. This operating expense fee shall
automatically and without further action increase annually at the rate of an
additional twenty-five cents ($0.25) per one thousand (1,000) gallons of water
metered commencing on March 1, 2022. Like increases of twenty-five cents
($0.25) per thousand gallons of water metered shall occur on March 1 of each
year thereafter, unless modified by action of the board of trustees.
   (B)   Multiple Connection User Charges: In addition to the rates and charges
in subsection (A) of this section, each multiple connection user shall pay
additional per unit charges after the first unit, as follows:
      1.   One dollar fifty cent ($1.50) capital assessment fee; and
      2.   Twenty cent ($0.20) debt service fee.
   (C)   Special Multiple Connection User Charges: A special multiple
connection user shall pay a multiple charge equal to the total number of beds
contained in a special multiple connection user facility divided by the average
dwelling unit size of 2.7 residents per household rounded to the next whole
number times the rates and charges specified in subsection (A) of this section.
(For example, a 100 bed nursing home shall be charged for 37 multiples.) In any
event, each special multiple connection user shall be charged a minimum of four
(4) multiples of the rates and charges in subsection (A) of this section.
   (D)   Minimum Bimonthly Rates And Charges: Each account per single meter
shall pay a minimum amount equal to eight thousand (8,000) gallons of water
usage per bimonthly period and no credit shall be provided for any unused water
amount.
   (E)   Fire Protection District: The Fire Protection District shall pay the
rates and charges pursuant to the intergovernmental agreement between the Fire
Protection District and the Village.
   (F)   Estimate Of Water Used: The water used for which rates and methods of
measurement are not specifically provided for by ordinance shall be estimated
by the Village and assessed at the then current rate specified herein for each
one thousand (1,000) gallons used rounded up to the next thousand, however,
whenever practical a meter shall be used as the basis of such estimate. (Ord.
1053, 11-14-2006; amd. Ord. 1342, 2-8-2021)
12-3-2: NEW WATER ACCOUNT FEE:
A new account fee of twenty five dollars ($25.00) shall be paid to the Village
for meter reading and administrative expenses, except when the water meter
charge is paid pursuant to section
12-3-5 of this chapter. This fee may be added to the first water bill of the
new account. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-3-3: ADDITIONAL WATER METERS:
Where more than one water meter is required by a multiple- family residential
unit, the contractor, developer, or property owner shall pay the cost for the
additional water meters. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-3-4: PERMIT FEES AND INSPECTION FEES:
   (A)   Permit Fee: The permit fee for connection with any water main shall be
as follows:
      1.   Single-Family Residence: Four thousand two hundred eighty three
dollars ($4,283.00) (including water meter, buffalo box, curb stop and outside
meter reading dial);
      2.   Multi-Family Residential Building: Four thousand two hundred eighty
three dollars ($4,283.00) per living unit in each multi-family residential
building (including water meter, buffalo box, curb stop and outside meter
reading dial); and

      3.   Commercial And Industrial Buildings: The fee for a commercial or

   (B)   Inspection Fee:

      2.   All funds derived from the application of the connection charges

12-3-5: WATER METER NEW ACCOUNT CHARGE:
A water meter new account charge of fifty dollars ($50.00) per residential
customer and one hundred dollars ($100.00) for commercial, institutional, and
industrial customers shall be billed for each new account, for a change of
name, and for a change of address. The amount billed shall be included on the
first billing following the establishment of the new account, change of name,
and/or change of address. (Ord. 1297, 11-13-2018)
12-3-6: FEES FOR CONTRACTORS' USE OF WATER:
In the event a contractor wishes to connect to the waterworks system for the
purposes of obtaining water for construction activity located in the Village
limits, the Village shall require a one hundred dollar ($100.00) deposit and
charge ten dollars ($10.00) per day for daily usage plus two hundred percent
(200%) of the current water rates and charges. In addition, any contractor
connecting to the Village's waterworks system on a temporary basis shall sign
an indemnity form, releasing the Village from any liability as a result of the
connection to the waterworks system as provided on the form entitled "Agreement
for Contractor's Use of Water System" and agree to be bound by the terms
contained therein. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)
12-3-7: METER TESTING CHARGE:
In the event that a water customer claims that a water meter is defective, said
meter may be tested by a certified lab by the Village with the cost of such
test being borne by the water customer after the water customer signs a written
agreement and pays the cost in advance of the test being conducted. The water
customer is entitled to all reports and a refund of the test cost in the event
that the meter is defective. (Ord. 1053, 11-14-2006)

   ORDINANCE: This title.
